pr_comments: Would be nice if we had a `Join pane into previous` or even a `Join pane into direction` so we could pass `next`, `prev`, left` or `right`. Is there a reason this was only implemented for a single direction?

issue_context.title: Join/merge panes
issue_context.body:
### Discussed in https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/discussions/12115
Originally posted by **tcard** May 22, 2024 In VSCode, "View: Join Editor Group With Next Group" does the equivalent of (in Zed terms) moving all open files from a pane to the next pane and then closing the pane. This allows you to keep working with fewer panes, while keeping all of the current open files and without having to worry about their state of save. This is a feature I miss while using Zed.
comments:
I think this is especially valuable now that you can hide the tab bar - because you're not aware of how many tabs you might be closing when you run "close inactive items" - I'd love to work with panes without worrying about getting the popup asking if I want to discard unsaved changes

looks like this is also related to https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/issues/5182

review_comments:
I'm conflicted about this. There is already a notion of "next pane" in `activate_next_pane`, meaning "next in the pane group's internal vector, wrapping around at the end". This typically follows the order in which the pane were created.

I tried reusing that notion of "next" for this action, but I found it better UX to have a predictable direction for the join purely based on relative position rather than history. It's also what VSCode does.

Unfortunately this complicates the "close pane if no items left on it". Normally, after closing the current pane, it focuses on the previous pane. But for this action, we need to focus on the pane we're joining into. So we optionally pass the pane to focus on through the close pane flow, which involves several methods and events.

As for joining direction, this order of preference reproduces VSCode's. I'm not particularly attached to it, as long as it's predictable.

To me, clockwise order is what I've also imagined.
After playing with it, seems that it's nice to have it this way too, thank you for the explanations.
